result.title: AVCORP: Identifying and Resisting Deception via Communication Theory and Theory of Mind
result.comment: 36 pages (with appendix), 17 figures, 24 tables. Code and corpus: https://github.com/fardinsaad/_AVCORP_ . Dataset and detector: https://huggingface.co/collections/fardinsaad/avcorp
result.summary: Today's LLM-based agents are vulnerable to deception by users and other agents. Defending against deception requires Theory of Mind (ToM) reasoning to infer the beliefs and goals of others as well as modeling tactics based on communication theory. To enable training models to detect deception, we adopt the well-known deception game, Avalon. We present a corpus, AVCORP, of 5,000 annotated utterances from 250 games of Avalon. AVCORP includes (1) 37 tactics mapped to a 4x4 behavior matrix, and (2) reasoning traces capturing abductive hypotheses, suspicion levels, and nested ToM beliefs. We train Qwen3-8B on AVCORP and evaluate it on 25 held-out games and 20 games played by humans. On held-out games, our best trained detector outperforms its untrained baseline and frontier models (GPT-5.6 Sol, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek-V4-Pro), matching Claude Opus 5.5. On human games, every trained detector exceeds the untrained model in F1 score across all rounds.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 Avalon 欺骗检测语料 AVCORP（5,000 条标注话语，含 37 种战术与行为矩阵、推测性假设与嵌套 ToM 信念的推理轨迹），并用其训练 Qwen3-8B 检测器，在留出对局与真人对局上优于未训练基线及部分前沿模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 属纯文本社会推理、无视觉输入，但其把怀疑度、嵌套信念等信念状态显式写入中间轨迹并加以监督，可能为 LVR 中显式信念/证据状态如何表示、更新与训练提供概念参照，可供核查。
